alerts.title: Carbamazepine contraindicated with DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines list carbamazepine as a contraindication for DTG and state it decreases DTG levels by 30–70%. The patient started carbamazepine 2 weeks ago while on TLD. Viral load was suppressed (<50 copies/mL) in September 2025 but is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This strongly suggests DTG levels have been reduced by carbamazepine, leading to virological failure. Guidelines recommend using valproic acid instead.

evidence.recommended_action: Stop carbamazepine and switch to valproic acid or another compatible antiepileptic. Repeat viral load after 3 months. If persistently detectable, proceed to genotype testing.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatremia
alerts.message: The patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), with symptoms of ataxia, nystagmus, and tremor. Hyponatremia (sodium 128 mmol/L) is also consistent with carbamazepine toxicity. The clinician plans dose reduction and repeat level, which is appropriate. Concurrent valproate may complicate management. ALT 68 U/L is mildly elevated; both carbamazepine and valproate can cause hepatotoxicity, though the elevation is modest.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat level and sodium. Monitor ALT. Consider neurology review for dual antiepileptic therapy and potential simplification.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load needs adherence and genotype plan
alerts.message: Guidelines define suppressed as ≤200 copies/mL. This patient's viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL. The primary cause is likely the carbamazepine–DTG interaction reducing DTG levels. The clinician's plan does not address enhanced adherence counselling or a repeat viral load after correcting the interaction. Guidelines recommend genotype testing if viraemia persists after addressing adherence and interactions.

evidence.recommended_action: After switching from carbamazepine, provide enhanced adherence counselling and repeat viral load in 3 months. If still detectable, perform genotype testing.
